import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Create a boxplot to visualize the distribution of transaction amounts by fraud status
sns.boxplot(x='is_fraud', y='amount', data=data, palette="Set2")

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amount Distribution by Fraud Status', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Is Fraud', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks([0, 1], ['Not Fraud', 'Fraud'], fontsize=12)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axis
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Create a boxplot to visualize the distribution of transaction amounts by fraud status
sns.boxplot(x='is_fraud', y='amount', data=data, palette="Set2")

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amount Distribution by Fraud Status', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Is Fraud', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks([0, 1], ['Not Fraud', 'Fraud'], fontsize=12)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
